Chapter 5: Building Community and Finding Fulfillment in Service
You know, one of our deepest needs is to feel like we belong. We all want to be part of something bigger, to know that our presence actually matters in the grand scheme of things. For her, community wasn’t just the setting for her story—it was the very soil where her sense of purpose took root and flourished.
Over decades of teaching, mentoring, and volunteering, she discovered something powerful. When you give your time and energy to others, you don’t just help them—you build bonds that can last a lifetime.
Early on in her career, she joined a group dedicated to helping students from all kinds of backgrounds. It was tough work—long hours, lots of challenges, and plenty of creative thinking required. But the rewards? They were unforgettable. She watched young people, some wrestling with self-doubt or tough situations, find their footing and begin to shine. The pride she felt wasn’t about what she’d accomplished—it was about seeing real change happen. It was witnessing what’s possible when people get the support and encouragement they truly need.
And her service didn’t stop at the classroom doors. Out in the wider community, she got involved in projects to fight poverty, support education, and bring people together across divides. Sure, there were setbacks. Some projects didn’t go as planned, and even well-intentioned folks sometimes disagreed. But through it all, she learned the value of sticking with it. Lasting change rarely happens overnight, but those small, steady efforts—they stack up over time.
The relationships she built through service? They became some of the most meaningful in her life. Colleagues turned into friends, and friends became like family. Working shoulder to shoulder toward a shared goal brought everyone closer—differences in background or belief just faded into the background. It became so clear: real fulfillment isn’t something you find when you’re alone. It’s something you discover in connection—with others, with a common purpose, and with the world around you.
Here’s something to think about. Most people underestimate the difference they can make. They figure, “Well, I’m not in charge, so what can I do?” But her experience taught her the opposite. Every act of service—no matter how small—sends out ripples, touching lives in ways you might never even see. And over time, those ripples add up. They become a legacy, a living testament to what’s possible when you choose to live for something greater than yourself.
